new_exact_applications.exact_application: Sections 3--7 define compact degree on a real complete normed space; hypotheses H in section12 and entire sections13--15 give homotopy invariance and existence from nonzero degree. Apply on the open C(P1,R) ball of radius osc(Q)+1. The independently constructed normalized T_t is collectively compact on the closed ball for t in [0,lambda], uniformly continuous in t there (uniform density bounds, compact Green images and uniform Taylor expansion at zero), and has no boundary fixed point by the canonical curve barriers. T_0 is a constant map with its fixed point strictly inside the ball, so I-T_0 has degree1 by finite-dimensional reduction and translation. Nonzero degree at lambda gives a genuine continuous solution. The stronger connected-continuum conclusion of section16 is unnecessary. Finite-dimensional Brouwer degree is the separately imported foundation; no recursive certification of all its literature is asserted.

The whole bounded Lemma1.2 proof supports the equality-set maximum inequality at bounded truncations. The full condition(B) setup, Theorem1.5 statement and proof, and Corollary1.6 proof are read. Every positive smooth Hermitian H satisfies(B) with a finite B>0, after harmless positive operator scaling. For bounded p,r and MA_H(p)<=k MA_H(r) on {p<r}, k<1, normalize -L<=r<=0; choose tau so (1-tau)^N>k and m_tau<0, and then choose s>0 small enough for the exact s<tau^3/[32B(N-1)^2] bound and D(1-tau)^N>k. On the nonempty strict comparison set contained in {p<r}, MA_H((1-tau)r)>=(1-tau)^N MA_H(r)+tau^N H^N. The modified comparison estimate would force this strict set to have zero smooth volume, contradicting the local submean/usc property of genuine bounded quasi-psh representatives. This proves the required bounded ratio domination without BMP or uniform v_minus>0. Corollary1.6 is not used as a uniform lower mass bound. Extra-pole and infinite-mass competitors are handled only by bounded max(v,U-k) and finite-level locality, not by a global unbounded maximum-product theorem.

new_exact_applications.exact_application: The bounded proof of Theorem3.5 and entire section6 through Theorem6.9 are read, including propositions6.1--6.5, Corollary6.6, and the full Josefson6.8 and polar/capacity6.9 proofs. On relatively compact curve coordinate disks, continuous Q plus a smooth local FS potential is a bounded subharmonic function. Normalize it between0 and1 on the disk; its actual degree-one measure is bounded by a constant times the relative BT capacity by the capacity definition. Polar Borel sets have outer capacity zero by6.9, so the actual mu charges none. Charts cover the curve, and genuine slicing plus smooth-factor Fubini proves product non-pluripolarity. No boundedness assertion is imported for the arbitrary nonpolar branch F.
